title: lepechinia bullata
intro: Lepechinia bullata, commonly known as Mountain Balm, is a perennial plant species belonging to the Lamiaceae family. It is used in traditional medicine for its health benefits, which include anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and antiseptic properties. The bioactive constituents present in Mountain Balm include volatile oils, flavonoids, and phenolic acids, which contribute to its therapeutic actions such as wound healing, pain relief, and digestive issues. The plant's therapeutic actions include its ability to soothe skin irritations, reduce fever, and exhibit antioxidant properties.
